import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 258

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)
- [St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
-/

namespace Erdos258

/--
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean"]
theorem erdos_258 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : answer(True) ↔ ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ),
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos258

findings.description: The docstring cites “[ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13.” In that paper, (2.13) is a displayed inequality in the proof of Lemma 2.2, not a theorem. The general monotone result is Theorem 2.23. The Lean statement itself is mathematically correct.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős and Straus, Some number theoretic results, Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971), https://msp.org/pjm/1971/36-3/pjm-v36-n3-p07-s.pdf: equation (2.13) appears on p. 640; Theorem 2.23 on p. 641 states irrationality whenever 2 ≤ a₁ ≤ a₂ ≤ ⋯, combining Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13” with “Theorem 2.23” (or cite Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14).

status_issues.recorded: An unconditional `formal_proof using lean4` annotation at [St26], together with `research solved` and `answer(True)`.
status_issues.source_status: The affirmative solution is correctly recorded as solved. However, the exact linked Lean development is only a conditional formalization: it assumes the Tao–Teräväinen theorem as a custom axiom. Although the problem website also labels the result PROVED (LEAN), the linked proof itself explicitly documents this limitation.
status_issues.evidence: The cited gist's introduction says the proof is “modulo the deep Tao–Teräväinen theorem ... (stated here without proof).” Lines 306–314 explicitly introduce `axiom tao_teravainen`; `tao_teravainen_divisors_le` uses it, and the final `erdos_258` uses that lemma. After adapting only proof tactics for the sandbox's newer Lean version, `#print axioms erdos_258` reports `[propext, tao_teravainen, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. Exact source: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep `research solved` and `answer(True)`. Record the formalization as `conditional formal_proof ... assuming ...`, with a same-file declaration stating the assumed Tao–Teräväinen multiplicity-counting bound Ω(N+k) ≤ Ck. Qualify the docstring accordingly. Alternatively, remove the unconditional formal-proof annotation until a complete formal proof is linked.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires 2 ≤ a n for every natural index, whereas the source permits arbitrary positive integers at the positive indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given a source-admissible sequence, set b(n)=max(2,a(n)). Since a(n)→∞, a and b agree beyond some N. Write Q_a(N)=∏_{i=1}^N a_i and similarly for b. Both series converge, and S_a=r+q S_b, where q=Q_b(N)/Q_a(N) is a nonzero rational and r is the rational difference of the corresponding finite prefixes. Thus S_a is irrational exactly when S_b is. The converse implication follows by restriction to sequences with entries at least 2. The unused a(0) causes no restriction on the positive-index sequence. This universal-statement equivalence is proved as main_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using any admitted conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Lean imposes the lower bound and monotonicity on all of ℕ; the source's monotone specialization concerns positive-index sequences of positive integers tending to infinity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a source-admissible nondecreasing sequence, choose b(0)=2 and b(n)=max(2,a(n)) for n≥1. Then b is nondecreasing on all of ℕ, every entry is at least 2, and b agrees with a eventually. The same nonzero rational scaling plus rational finite-prefix correction preserves irrationality. Conversely, restrict a Lean-admissible sequence to positive indices. Proved as monotone_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, using MonotoneOn a (Set.Ici 1) for the source's monotonicity condition.

review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalization was found in the three declarations. Lean inspection confirms real division and the intended products over indices 1 through n+1. Scratch proofs establish nonzero denominators and summability, using d(n) ≤ n and products ≥ 2^n, so the default value of a divergent tsum is unreachable. Small divisor counts, products and rational summands were tested. The equivalence and summability proofs compile with only standard axioms. The external proof's compatibility-adjusted copy is /workspace/review/sourcecheck-adapted.lean; its definitions and theorem statements were unchanged.
